ship: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

ship.header: Captain's log, stardate 80240.8. Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse; the list carries no tagged version.
ship.situation: We are at Alex's house on Moraga Way in Orinda, on the evening of Friday the twenty-eighth. This was the third engagement of the evening of four, taken up after Edgar Markov left the line. Two vessels opposite, under Alex and under Stuart.
ship.narrative: The opening hand I chose to keep was a good one and dense with answers, and I spent them where I meant to; the ship did the thing it is built to do and lost anyway. The structural cost showed itself early: the card flow we generate is symmetric, so every card we hand ourselves we also hand to the vessels we are trying to answer, and they were never short of material with which to fight our counters. The game closed in a long exchange over a single spell. I answered a spell of theirs, Alex answered my answer, and when I cast Swords to Plowshares he redirected it onto Heliod. The engine was offline from that point forward. Psychosis Crawler stood on the battlefield with the pieces present to grow it, and we never arrived.

assessment.text: The design of this ship is mine and so is the fault in it. I have laid in too many separate lines of attack and provided none of them with cover; committing my removal into an open answer was an error of judgment on my part, but the deeper error was made long before the game, at the drawing board.

Two things about the vessel are now plain. The card flow is symmetric and arms the table at the rate it arms us, which is the archetype's own problem and not an accident of this list. And the whole engine rests on the commander, with nothing aboard that answers an exchange of counters followed by redirected removal. Losing Heliod ended our participation in the game.
Alex held the two answers the situation required and played them in the correct order. I do not find that remarkable; I find that it was available to him, which is the part that concerns me.

orders.text: I have ordered Tactical to place protection for the commander ahead of every other acquisition. Nothing further is added to this ship until it can survive a contested exchange over one spell.
I have instructed Helm to reduce the number of routes we are attempting to hold open at once and to choose among them rather than carry all of them thinly.
I have directed Ops to review the symmetry in our card flow, which at present supplies the table at the same rate it supplies us.

ship.coda: I am not persuaded that the concepts aboard are wrong; I am persuaded that there are too many of them for one hull. We refit, and we go out again with fewer errands and better cover.
